# How to Use Google's Latest AI Updates to Organise Your Daily Life

Imagine having a personal assistant that doesn't just answer questions, but actually remembers your preferences, organises your hectic schedule, and watches a quick home video to tell you how to fix a squeaky door. 

Google’s latest AI updates bring this closer to reality by embedding smart tools directly into the apps you already use every day. Here is how you can use these new features to simplify your life.

## From chatbots to "AI agents"

For a long time, using AI felt like chatting with a very smart textbook. You asked a question, and it wrote a reply. 

Now, the technology is moving toward **AI agents** (smart software assistants that can use digital tools and take real actions on your behalf, rather than just writing text). Instead of you copying and pasting information between your emails, spreadsheets, and calendar, these agents can connect the dots for you.

At the same time, these tools have become fully **multimodal** (the ability to process different types of information at the same time, like video, sound, and text). This means you can interact with the AI using whatever format makes sense in the moment.

## Smart searching with video and voice

One of the most practical upgrades is how you can search for help around the home. If you are struggling with a appliance or a tricky craft project, you no longer have to type long, confusing descriptions into a search bar.

Instead, you can open your Google app, hold down the search button, and record a short video of the object. While recording, you can simply ask out loud: *"Why is this lever not moving?"* 

The AI analyses the video and the audio together, identifies the exact model of your item, and searches the web to find the precise solution. It is like having an expert standing right next to you.

## Letting AI handle your life admin

We all have a digital paper trail of receipts, booking confirmations, and school newsletters scattered across our inboxes. Google's updated AI features make it much easier to organise this chaos.

Because of a massive **context window** (how much text or information the AI can hold in its active memory at one time), you can ask the AI to analyse years of emails in a second. 

For example, you can ask your assistant to:
- Find all the receipts from your recent home renovation and list them in a Google Sheet.
- Compare three different flight itineraries sent to your inbox and draft a calendar invite for the best option.
- Search your emails for school newsletters and create a checklist of key dates for the upcoming term.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: You can outsource tedious household planning. Instead of spending your Sunday evening comparing holiday accommodation emails or sorting through digital receipts, you can ask the AI to categorise and summarise them for you.
- **For your business or work**: You can automate repetitive tasks. If you use Google Workspace at work, you can ask the AI to summarise long email threads you missed while on leave, or draft client follow-ups based on rough meeting notes in Google Docs.
- **If you're just getting started**: Start small. The next time you need to find a specific piece of information buried in your emails—like an old policy number or a friend's dietary requirements—open Gemini in your browser or your Google app and ask: *"Find the email about..."*

## Wrap-up

AI is quickly moving from a tool we simply talk to, into a proactive helper that can take real work off our hands. By testing these new features in your daily routine, you can claw back valuable time for the things that actually matter to you. 

To take your first step today, open the Google app on your phone, tap the camera icon in the search bar, and try searching for an object in your room using a photo and a spoken question.
